WHAT YOU NEED TO DO Self-Starting
Don’t react to what’s happening around you. Act first to outperform your competitors!
DON’T copy competitors, you must offer something different.
If your circumstances are challenging, actively work to change them.
It is actions that turn ideas into reality - get up and do it!
Think before you act - random actions are useless.
But: Be quick – you’ve got to collect feedback before implementing actions

Training
6
EXERCISE
Instruction:
This exercise presents two case studies of women entrepreneurs in Kenya
The first female entrepreneur shows Get Up & Go! behaviour while the second
female entrepreneur shows Laid Back behaviour.
Form groups of Four (04) people to work on this exercise.
Groups A:
▪ Look at case 1 « Get Up & Go female entrepreneur".
▪ Identify and record what is proactive in their behaviour and the consequences
of this.
Groups B :
▪ Then look at case 2 « Laid Back female entrepreneur".
▪ Identify and note what is reactive in their behaviour and the consequences of
this.

Training
7
Hello, I am Annie. I produce and sell herbs from my region. Before that, I
worked in a food laboratory for four years. To learn how to run a business,
I regularly watch videos on the internet about accounting and
management. My business has grown steadily over the past few years. I
recently set myself the goal of doubling my turnover within a year. To get
higher prices for my products, I tried to contact a supermarket in Nairobi.
As no one responded to me, I asked a friend, who works for the
supermarket, to take a sample of my products to his manager. In this
way, I was able to attract the attention of the management and began
collaborating with the supermarket.
To deliver my products to the supermarket, I work with a local farmer, who
often travels to Nairobi. I’m also working to ensure my products are
certified 'organic’, because I believe organic products will be in greater
demand in the coming years and I will be able to get a better price for
them.
GET UP & GO! ENTREPRENEUR:
ANNIE

Training
8
Hello, my name is Pauline. I learned about the production and marketing of
herbs from my parents. When they got older, I took over their business and
basically stuck to their business routine because it worked okay for them. I
never really looked for new ways to do anything, like increase production or
improve marketing.
However, one of my main problems is packaging and selling my herbs. It
takes a long time to get into Nairobi to buy the packaging I need. As a
result, I avoid travelling if possible, but that means I can run out of boxes
and bags for my products. For the same reason, I don’t usually attend the
big trade markets where my competitors exhibit their products and look for
business partners. Slower sales also mean I lack space to store my
products. I can’t really think of anything I can do to change these
problems; I’m just hoping one day there will be a new road to Nairobi.
LAID BACK
ENTREPRENEUR:
PAULINE

EXERCISE Self-Starting
Example: Daily routine of a small grocery shop owner
Time Activities
8.00 Open the shop and put up the usual advertising outside the shop.
Wait for the first customer.
Telephone call from the supplier: he will not be able to deliver fresh fruit today.
This is already the third time this has happened in a fortnight. Hopefully it will get better
soon.
Customer service. Some people leave the shop without buying anything because they are
only looking for fresh fruit. Send these customers to the competitor on the next street.
Not many customers today, use the time to call friends and start chatting.
Cleaning of the shop front and signage.
Closing of the shop.
Counting sales and calculating turnover for today - a bad day...
Instruction:
Review this shop owner’s routine and identify where they should be more Go-Getting!

WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Being Future-Oriented
Think about future opportunities in the market and make notes on how you can
use them for your business.
Think about the barriers that might arise in the future and prepare for them
now.
Always anticipate long-term consequences before acting on future opportunities
and barriers.
